title: Chiral Graviton Modes in Non-Abelian lattice Fractional Quantum Hall states
authors: Zeno Bacciconi, Min Long, Hernan Xavier, Hongyu Lu, Marcello Dalmonte, Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Synthetic quantum matter provides a highly tunable route to fractional quantum Hall physics beyond the constraints of conventional electronic materials. However, previous theoretical studies have mostly focused on their ground state properties. It remains unclear to what extent such platforms could reveal key excitation properties of fractional quantum Hall states. Here, we study charge-neutral collective excitations in a non-abelian lattice fractional quantum Hall state realized in the bosonic Harper-Hofstadter model at unity filling factior, realizing a Moore-Read ground state. Combining full exact diagonalization, band-projected exact diagonalization, and matrix-product-state simulations, we demonstrate the existence of a long-lived chiral graviton mode, probed by chiral 3-body correlators, for the first time on lattice non-Abelian states. The graviton signal is topological sector-independent and could be observed via geometric quenches in small open droplets directly relevant to current cold-atom experiments, while other neutral modes, such as the magnetoroton and neutral fermion, are less resolved at presently achievable volumes.
summary: The paper investigates the collective excitations of non-Abelian lattice FQH states, focusing on the chiral graviton mode. Using advanced numerical simulations like MPS and ED, the authors successfully demonstrate the existence of this long-lived excitation using 3-body correlators. This work provides a key diagnostic tool for characterizing exotic topological phases relevant to modern quantum simulation experiments.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate key excitation properties, specifically the existence of a chiral graviton mode (CGM), in non-Abelian lattice Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) states beyond just their ground state characteristics.
main_result: The authors demonstrated the first observation of a long-lived chiral graviton mode using chiral 3-body correlators on lattice non-Abelian states, showing robustness across different geometries and topological sectors.
method: A combination of advanced numerical techniques was employed, including full exact diagonalization (fED), band-projected ED (pED), and Matrix Product State (MPS) simulations to calculate spectral densities from 3-body correlators.
model_or_system:
The system models non-Abelian FQH states using the bosonic Harper–Hofstadter model realized on a square lattice, specifically targeting the $
u=1$ Moore–Read ground state. The Hamiltonian includes hopping terms and three-body onsite interactions.
key_observables: Chiral graviton mode (CGM) spectrum, 3-body correlators ($O^{\pm}_{3b}$), spectral density $I^{\pm}_{3b}(\omega)$, and the intrinsic decay rate ($\Gamma_G$).
important_parameters: Low flux per plaquette ($\phi$), finite droplet sizes ($9 	imes 9$ disk), three-body interaction strength ($W$), and lattice geometry (disk, cylinder, torus).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the continuum stress tensor onto lattice operators and making approximations in spectral function analysis due to finite interactions or computational limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup involving the graviton operator, show the resolved CGM spectrum from MPS simulations on open disks, demonstrate real-time dynamics after geometric quenches, and compare spectra across different topological sectors.
paper_structure: The work progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using lattice Hamiltonians, then applying advanced numerical methods (ED/MPS) to calculate 3-body correlators, demonstrating the CGM signal's existence and robustness, and finally analyzing its lifetime via quench dynamics.
why_interesting: This bridges concepts from topological quantum matter (FQH states) with measurable excitation signatures (graviton modes), providing concrete predictions for experimental realization in cold atom platforms.
